The AAU is therefore inviting institutions of higher learning to nominate staff to participate in this high-level executive training. TITLE: IFAE researchers among winners of prestigious Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Researchers from the BIST Community centre IFAE are among the thousands of researchers worldwide honoured with the 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics, awarded to the ATLAS Collaboration at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider (LHC) alongside its sister experiments ALICE, CMS, and LHCb. Members of the ATLAS Collaboration in front of the ATLAS experiment mural (1:3 scale) and ATLAS control room located at CERN, 100 m above the experiment cavern. Credit: ATLAS Cllaboration / Struik, Michael ATLAS is one of the largest and most complex scientific instruments ever built. As a general-purpose particle detector measuring over 40 metres in length and around 25 metres in height, it was designed to investigate the fundamental building blocks of matter and the forces governing our universe. Its cutting-edge systems track particles produced in particle collisions at unprecedented energies, enabling discoveries like the Higgs boson and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. The Breakthrough Prize specifically highlights the ATLAS Collaboration’s significant contributions to particle physics, including detailed measurements of Higgs boson properties, studies of rare processes and matter-antimatter asymmetry, and the exploration of nature under the most extreme conditions. “The Breakthrough Prize is a testament to the dedication and ingenuity of the ATLAS Collaboration and our colleagues across the LHC experiments,” said ATLAS Spokesperson Stephane Willocq. “This prize recognises the collective vision and monumental effort of thousands of ATLAS collaborators worldwide.” “I am extremely proud to see the extraordinary accomplishments of the LHC collaborations honoured with this prestigious Prize,” said Fabiola Gianotti, Director-General of CERN. “It is a beautiful recognition of the collective efforts, dedication, competence and hard work of thousands of people from all over the world who contribute daily to pushing the boundaries of human knowledge.” IFAE has been at the forefront of ATLAS research since 1992, contributing to: • Design, construction and operation of the Tile Calorimeter (TileCal), critical for the reconstruction of collision events. • Development and validation of software used in the Trigger System, as well as its operation, enabling the efficient collection of data by the experiment. • Leadership in multiple physics working groups and the ATLAS Publication Committee, shaping the experiment’s scientific direction. • Design and development of the distributed computing system used by the collaboration to manage and analyze the ATLAS data. Operation of a Tier-1 center at PIC. “Our team’s work on the detector and trigger operation during Run 2, as well as the scientific exploitation of the experiment, exemplifies the innovation driving ATLAS forward,” said Aurelio Juste, ICREA Research Professor at IFAE. “This recognition affirms the impact of our contributions and inspires us to continue exploring the universe’s most fundamental questions,” indicated Imma Riu, Staff Researcher at IFAE. Aurelio Juste and Imma Riu are co-leading the ATLAS group at IFAE. “The successes of Run 2 showcase the ingenuity of the ATLAS Collaboration — not only in collecting data with a detector of outstanding precision, but also in our relentless drive to improve our understanding of it,” said Andreas Hoecker, former ATLAS Spokesperson. While the ATLAS Collaboration celebrates the recognition of the Breakthrough Prize, its focus remains firmly on the future. The third operation period of the LHC is currently underway and preparations for the High-Luminosity LHC upgrade are advancing rapidly. A team of about 10 physicists and engineers at IFAE is deeply involved in preparing ATLAS for its next chapter, led by Sebastian Grinstein, ICREA Research Professor at IFAE. They are leading the development of the Inner Tracker (ITk) and High Granularity Timing Detector (HGTD) for the High-Luminosity LHC, which will increase collision rates tenfold when it begins operation in 2030. “We are

Researchers from IFAE are among the winners of the 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics, awarded to the ATLAS Collaboration at CERN's Large Hadron Collider alongside ALICE, CMS, and LHCb.

TITLE: Application now open for the next competition of the Carnegie African Diaspora Fellowship Program (CADFP)

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
DEADLINE: September 30, 2022 at 11:59 PM EST The Institute of International Education (IIE) is pleased to announce that the next round of competition for the CADFP is now open. Apply now or share this message with those who might be interested. What is the CADFP? The CADFP is a scholar exchange program for African higher education institutions to host a diaspora scholar for 14-90 days for projects in curriculum co-development, research collaboration and graduate student teaching and mentoring. The Association of African Universities (AAU) is a partner of the Carnegie African Diaspora Fellowship Program. Who is eligible? Accredited universities in Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania and Uganda, and member institutions of the African Research Universities Alliance (ARUA) (including Addis Ababa University, Ethiopia; the University of Rwanda; Cheikh Anta Diop University, Senegal; and University of Mauritius) can submit a project request to host a scholar. Scholars born in Africa, who live in the United States or Canada and work in an accredited college or university in either of those two countries, can apply online to be placed on a roster of candidates for a fellowship. Scholars must hold a terminal degree in their field and may hold any academic rank. How do I apply? Links and information about the African host institution project request application, scholar roster application and review guidelines are posted on the CADFP website. Interested parties are invited to register for one of the informational webinars: Information for Diaspora Scholars, Webinar #1: Wednesday August 3 at 12 noon Eastern US Time Information for Potential Hosts, Webinar #1: Thursday, August 4 at 12 noon West Central Africa Standard Time Information for Diaspora Scholars, Webinar #2: Tuesday, August 23 at 2:00 PM Eastern US Time Information for Potential Hosts, Webinar #2: Wednesday, August 24 at 2:00 PM West Central Africa Time After the webinars, a recording will be posted on the IIE’s YouTube Channel. Timeline The deadline for project requests from host universities and scholar applications for diaspora scholars is September 30, 2022 at 11:59 pm EST. Selection decisions will be made in October-November 2022; project visits can begin as early as January 1, 2023 and must be completed by November 30, 2023. Benefits Selected fellows receive a $150/day stipend, visa costs, limited health insurance, round-trip international air travel and ground transportation costs to and from home and the U.S./Canadian airport. Selected Host Fellows and Diaspora Fellows can apply for supplemental funds to be used for fieldwork, publication costs and workshops. The CADFP Team manages the fellowships and payments to fellows. Host institutions are encouraged to provide cost-share for the fellow’s meals, lodging and in-country transportation. For more information on the fellowship program and application process, as well as the projects of current fellows, please write to AfricanDiaspora@iie.org visit the Programme website and communities on Facebook and Twitter. The program is made possible by a grant from Carnegie Corporation of New York. Please contact: Carnegie African Diaspora Fellowship Program (CADFP) Institute of International Education (IIE) Email: africandiaspora@iie.org http://www.iie.org/AfricanDiaspora IIE • The Power of International Education

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Opportunities Circle is here with another great opportunity, “Commonwealth PhD Scholarships 2027-28.” Applications are open for fully funded PhD Scholarships in UK for students from Least Developed Countries and the vulnerable Commonwealth States. The UK scholarship is an excellent opportunity for international students who want to pursue their PhD abroad for free. Commonwealth Scholarships 2027 support all brilliant and outstanding applicants from least developing countries who cannot afford to study abroad otherwise. This fully funded UK scholarship will allow students to acquire the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to achieve sustainable development goals. This scholarship in UK will also help them to develop their leadership skills and become leaders in their home countries. Commonwealth Scholarships 2027-28 allow students from diverse backgrounds, countries, and races to apply for these fully funded PhD scholarships. Furthermore, these scholarships in UK also aim to promote cooperation and collaboration among nations. Similarly, this PhD scholarship is open for six themes: Improving health systems and capacity, Science and technology for development, Promoting innovation and entrepreneurship, Strengthening resilience and response to crises, Access, inclusion, and opportunity, and Strengthening global peace, security, and governance. The fully funded CSC Scholarship doesn’t require IELTS or any other English language certificate. However, different UK universities require IELTS or another English language certificate, depending on the country. The UK Commonwealth Scholarship is a merit-based scholarship, and the selection depends on academic merit, quality of the study plan, and prospective effect on the development of their home country. This Commonwealth PhD scholarship 2027 is a life-changing opportunity for students of least developed countries. Through these international PhD scholarships, they will be able to develop their personalities while studying at one of the top institutes. Students will also get to enhance their research capacity. Furthermore, the CSC PhD scholarships will provide full financial support for international students. The fully funded PhD scholarships cover the full tuition fee, return airfare, living stipend, accommodation, and a grant for international academic-related travel. Scholarships for International Students UK will help students boost their educational careers and polish their skills, which will be a valuable addition to their professional careers. Commonwealth PhD Scholarships (low income countries) are funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office (FCDO), which enable talented and motivated individuals from different parts of the world to gain the knowledge and skills that are necessary for sustainable development and are aimed at those who otherwise could not afford to study in UK. The Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan (CSFP) is one of the world’s most prestigious scholarship schemes. The Commonwealth Scholarship Scheme was established in 1959; these Commonwealth scholarships or fellowships have been granted to more than 30,000 people; 28,500 of these were funded by the UK government through the UK Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC). TITLE: Invitation to In-person Training Workshop (Institutional Repositories) in Zanzibar, Tanzania

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
22 -25 August, 2022 Theme: Restructuring Institutional Repositories to support teaching learning and research The covid-19 pandemic has shown why it is urgent that African Universities have E-content in our institutions to support the academic environment. The covid-19 pandemic exposed our inadequacy in having enough E-resources to support virtual learning/teaching in African HEIs. African HEIs and their students had no online resources they could rely on. The need to have online E-content has also been further highlighted by the unfortunate fire outbreaks that has destroyed the physical content of some HEIs on the continent. It is time for all in the knowledge management cycle Creators (researchers) and Managers (Information Professionals) to critically look at building strong platforms to support E-content development and make them available online to support the HEIs core mandates (teaching, learning and research) of our HEIs. It is to help reduce this inadequacy that the Association of African universities is collaborating with the Africa Digital Libraries Support Network and cordially invites you to a workshop on strengthening Institutional Repositories to provide the platform for building a critical mass of E-content for our institutions. This is an in-person training workshop and participants are expected to be onsite. Why in-person workshop? The workshop is totally hands-on with on-site guidance for real time implementation Experience from previous hands-on training shows participants coming with computers that require fixing because of the different operating systems, before it can be used in the training (this fixing is difficult to carry out online) There will be a day when each participating institution will have personal reviews of plans and also repository reviews for institutions that have an existing platform Who should attend the workshop? Directors of Research, Researchers, Librarians, IT Staff supporting Libraries, and Information Professionals. Institutions with the following challenges are especially encouraged to attend. Institutions with repositories that had gone silent in the wake of the covid19 pandemic. Institutions that have been unable to update their repositories for earlier versions Institutions having problems with the making their repositories harvestable Institutions having challenges with their advocacy and copyright policies For institutions having difficulty with digitizing records for upload unto their repositories The workshop will also provide the avenue to discuss taking steps to safeguard our physical collections against disasters. Participants will be required to attend the workshop with a laptop. Those coming from institutions with repositories should have administrative access to their institutional repository. There will be 2 days dedicated to holding clinics with each participating institution, where their repository will be reviewed with them. Institutions looking to setting up their repositories are also welcomed to attend Covid19 Protocols will be strictly adhered to in all sessions The Rate is $500 per participant for AAU members in good standing and $600 for Non-Members (Covers conference package which include meals, conference venue, certificates and conference material) The Registration Link is made available here https://event-mgt.aau.org/event/52/ For any further information, please contact Abednego Corletey (acorletey@aau.org); +233264655185 (Whatsapp only) NB: There will be a discussion on a provision now available for institutions to host their repositories free on the cloud. These institutions will be supported to setup their institutional repositories

TITLE: New UNESCO Global Education Monitoring Report Fellowship

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
A new UNESCO Global Education Monitoring Report Fellowship programme has just been launched thanks to the support of the Open Society Foundations. The Fellowship aims to strengthen the evidence base on comparative education. The first call for fellowships is online with applications expected by September 28. Such calls will be issued twice a year with the aim of hosting an average of three fellows per year in the team. Fellowships will typically provide or contribute to the funding for fellows to conduct their research and build their networks for one year, of which at least one month would be spent at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris. Based on the successful model of the Thomas J. Alexander Fellowships at the OECD, the GEM Report Fellowship programme will support academic researchers and research-oriented policy makers to carry out studies in the area of international and comparative education with a special focus on: utilizing the GEM Report’s data resources, notably those household and school surveys linked to the World Inequality in Education database, to strengthen analyses of global, regional and national education trends on issues of access, equity, inclusion and quality; strengthening the content of the GEM Report with respect to its coverage of important issues at the regional and national level, through evidence-based analyses of educational policy and practice; helping advance the SDG 4 monitoring agenda, especially on issues related to the global and thematic indicator framework that have been highlighted in previous reports; and supporting the themes of forthcoming GEM reports, i.e. inclusive education in 2020(including a special focus on (i) disability (ii) Latin America) and the role of non-state actors in education in 2021. The fellowships are open to exceptional individuals who have quantitative research skills, demonstrate a potential for transformational impact in their domain, and share a commitment to provide more people with better educational opportunities. Learning from their experience with the team, the fellows will also be able to participate in and influence the work of the GEM Report. A stipend of up to $25,000 for the duration of the fellowship and full travel costs for at least one month to be spent in Paris will be provided to each of the fellows. Please share the news with your networks and visit the online call for proposals to find out more.

TITLE: eLearning Summit 2025: Strengthening Digital Education in Africa Through Quality, Collaboration, and Workforce Development

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Press Release – Accra, Ghana (March 19, 2025) – The Association of African Universities (AAU), in collaboration with eLearnAfrica, is excited to announce the eLearning Summit 2025, scheduled to take place virtually on April 17, 2025, at 1 PM GMT / 3 PM SAST. Click to register here: https://forms.gle/W6VwJ3GFNoyWQenx8 The summit will bring together higher education leaders, policymakers, instructional designers, edtech innovators, and industry experts to explore strategies for expanding digital learning opportunities across Africa under the theme “Transforming Online Learning in Africa: Scaling Quality, Partnerships, and Workforce Development through Digital Education“. Following the success of the inaugural eLearning Summit in 2024, this edition will focus on enhancing the quality of online programmes, fostering impactful partnerships, and aligning digital education with Africa’s workforce development needs. Launch Event on AAU Talks As part of the build-up to the summit, the event will be launched on AAU Talks on AAUTV on Thursday, 20th March 2025, at 1 PM GMT / 2 PM SAST. The launch will provide deeper insights into key issues surrounding e-learning in Africa and set the stage for discussions leading up to the main event. What to Expect The eLearning Summit 2025 will feature high-level discussions, expert insights, and practical solutions aimed at strengthening Africa’s digital education landscape. Participants can expect engaging keynote addresses, thought-provoking panel discussions, and case study presentations from leading universities and industry experts. One of the summit’s highlights will be case studies showcasing successful implementations of online MBA programs and professional development courses. Universities that have effectively developed and scaled their online programs, increased student enrollments, and enhanced digital learning infrastructure will share their experiences. These presentations and panel discussions will offer valuable insights into best practices, challenges faced, and strategies for ensuring sustainability in online education. This free virtual summit is open to educators, administrators, policymakers, and all stakeholders committed to advancing online education in Africa. Attendees will have the opportunity to learn from thought leaders, discover innovative solutions for improving online learning quality and accessibility, explore partnership opportunities to enhance institutional capabilities, and gain insights into workforce needs and how digital education can bridge the skills gap. Click to register here: https://forms.gle/W6VwJ3GFNoyWQenx8 AAU and eLearnAfrica Partnership In 2016, eLearnAfrica entered into a partnership with the Association of African Universities (AAU), the largest higher education coordinating body in Africa, representing over 430 member universities across the continent. This collaboration aims to provide online, distance-learning opportunities to over 10 million African students, supporting universities in expanding their reach. The partnership has made significant strides, now boasting over 140 registered users(universities, institutions, as well as individual professors and course holders). It has successfully designed, developed, delivered, and deployed three master’s degree programs and over 200 short courses in collaboration with institutions such as Rhodes Business School and Njala University. For further information or inquiries about this partnership, please contact: aaulms@aau.org / isaack@elearnafrica.com / admin@elearnafrica.com .

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The “Doctoral Student Handbook” serves as the handbook of graduate policies and procedures. It contains academic information such as breadth and specialty requirements, General Exam information, time lines of satisfactory progress and thesis information. It also contains research information regarding funding, switching groups and other policies/procedures. Fall 2026 Written Exam Schedule The Physics Written Exams will be given as 4 separate sections. Incoming students must sit all exams unless they have a waiver from the Associate Department Head. Continuing students are required to sit those exams that they have not yet passed, unless they have passed a course, with a grade of B+ or higher, that fulfills that core requirement (8.309 for CM, 8.311 for EM, 8.321 for QM, and 8.333 for SM) or receive a waiver from the Associate Department Head. Upcoming Exam Dates Fall 2026 – August 31 and September 1 Introduction This document describes the doctoral program in the Physics Department. It supplements the MIT OGE Graduate Policies and Procedures, which outlines the general Institute requirements. The primary goals of the graduate program in physics at MIT are to solidify and broaden your knowledge of physics and to teach you how to do research, how to identify important problems, and how to communicate scientific information effectively. In short, you will be trained to become a professional physicist and a productive member of the scientific community. The major steps involved in your graduate career are described in the various sections here. The Physics Graduate Program The physics graduate program is under the direction of the Physics Education Committee, which includes members with the following graduate responsibilities: Prof. Scott Hughes, Associate Department Head Prof. Mehran Kardar, General Examination and Requirements Coordinator Prof. Christoph Paus, Graduate Appointments Coordinator Prof. William Detmold, Graduate Student Coordinator, Graduate Officer Ms. Shannon Larkin, Assistant Director, Academic Programs Ms. Jenni Roesch, Graduate Coordinator The staff in Academic Programs, Room 4-315, can direct you to committee members most appropriate to your specific questions or concerns. All graduate students and faculty are affiliated with one of the Department’s four research divisions. Each division is headed by a faculty member with responsibilities for aspects of the graduate program of that division’s students. The current Division Heads are: Prof. Raymond Ashoori, Atomic, Bio-, Condensed Matter, and Plasma Physics Prof. Anna Frebel, Astrophysics Prof. Gunther Roland, Experimental Nuclear and Particle Physics Prof. Tracy Slatyer, Theoretical Nuclear and Particle Physics Professor Scott Hughes serves as the advisor for student concerns about scientific misconduct issues including interactions with research supervisors, data integrity, and authorship. In addition, Physics REFS can provide mediation services between student peers and/or faculty members and Shannon Larkin, Assistant Director, can be helpful in dealing with sensitive issues. Every incoming student is assigned an academic advisor. Under most circumstances this faculty member will continue to advise the student until graduation. Later, when the student joins a research group, another faculty member will become his or her research supervisor. Thus, for most of their time in the Department, students have two separate faculty members to whom they can turn for help and advice. Throughout these guidelines, “advisor” refers to the academic advisor. The term “supervisor” is associated with the research or thesis supervisor, even though this person is often colloquially known as the “thesis advisor.” Types of Financial Support Note: For more detailed information regarding the cost of attendance, including specific costs for tuition and fees, books and supplies, housing and food as well as transportation, please visit the Student Financial Services (SFS) website. In sub-Saharan Africa, unique challenges and opportunities exist in aligning QA with meaningful impact. Interactive Discussions: Facilitated discussions to explore challenges and opportunities in institutional quality assurance. Case Studies: Real-world examples to illustrate the successful implementation of quality assurance for impact. Group Work and Exercises: Collaborative activities to apply learning to participants’ contexts. Action Plan Development: Guided sessions for participants to develop tailored action plans for their institutions. Be equipped with practical tools and methodologies to assess and enhance institutional impact. Gain insights into best practices and successful strategies from other institutions. Leave with a draft action plan to implement or improve quality assurance processes in their institutions. For further information, contact: obadinaw@aau.org and CC: lodzebe.gidisu@aau.org

TITLE: Call for host – AAU General Conference 2025

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
INTRODUCTION The Association of African Universities (AAU) will hold its 16th Quadrennial General Conference (QGC) in July 2025. The QGC, comprising representatives of members, associate members and observers, is the supreme authority of the Association and is responsible for determining the general policies of the Association. It is normally a five-day event centered around issues of relevance to higher education in Africa. The QGC comprises two parts; the first is the business session which evaluates the performance of the AAU in the preceding four years and approves of the programmes for the subsequent four years. The business session also incorporates the election of a new 15-member Board to steer the affairs of the Association for the next four years. The second part of the QGC is the scientific discussions of the theme and sub-themes of the Conference under the biennial Conference of Rectors, Vice-Chancellors and Rectors of African Universities (COREVIP). At the 16th General Conference, the 23rd COREVIP will be held. These events are jointly organised by the AAU and a member institution in good standing with the Association (i.e. having zero arrears in annual subscription payment). It should be noted that the co-hosting of this most important event on the calendar of the African higher education community provides very high-level visibility and exposure to the host institution and country because of the calibre and number of academic leaders, policymakers, researchers, development partners, industry, and other stakeholders that usually attend it, and it is, therefore, a highly sought-after event. 2025 QGC THEME Yet to be finalized. CALL FOR HOST The AAU hereby invites applications from member institutions for the co-hosting of this prestigious quadrennial Conference. The Host’s Responsibilities The host university will be expected to contribute to the organisation of the Conference, financially or in kind, in the areas of: Local transportation for participants. Airport “meet and greet” (reception and facilitation of immigration procedures). Traditional items as gifts to presenters and sessional chairs. Welcome Reception or Dinner for participants. Publicity and media coverage (local press, radio and TV, conference photographer). Arrangement of courtesy calls by the Governing Board on appropriate government authorities in the host country. Arrangement of excursion visits by delegates. Providing the Secretariat for the Conference (equipment and supplies). Decorations, banners, invitations to Opening/Closing Ceremony and receptions. Cultural display during open and closing ceremonies. Institutions interested in co-hosting the 16th Quadrennial General Conference should officially apply by filling this form: https://www.research.net/r/HostAAUGC25 The deadline for the receipt of the official application is Friday, 28, June 2024. View the photo gallery of some past AAU QGC and COREVIP below: – COREVIP hosted in Namibia: https://www.flickr.com/photos/aau-africa/albums/72177720309838569/ – QGC/COREVIP hosted in Egypt: https://www.flickr.com/photos/aau-africa/albums/72157710614218221/with/48647480413

TITLE: AAPAM and eLearnLXD Announce Scholarship Opportunities for Online Master’s in Public Administration

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The African Association for Public Administration and Management (AAPAM), in partnership with eLearnLXD, is pleased to announce scholarship opportunities for eligible AAPAM members in good standing to pursue the Online Master’s in Public Administration (MPA) offered by the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN). This partnership responds to the growing demand for accessible, flexible, and high-quality postgraduate education for public servants and managers across Africa. It represents a shared commitment to advancing professional excellence, innovation, and leadership in public administration through digitally enabled learning and training. Bridging the Skills Gap in Africa’s Public Sector During his presentation at the Academic Leadership Summit (ALS) – 2024, Prof. George Scott, Secretary General of AAPAM, underscored the urgency of strengthening professional development systems across the continent. “Africa faces various challenges in professional development, including limited access to quality training programmes, budget constraints, inadequate infrastructure, and a lack of skilled trainers. As a result, effective service delivery remains a challenge,” Prof. Scott noted. “Public servants, we all know, play a vital role in shaping the continent’s development trajectory. They are the backbone of any government, implementing policies, delivering essential services such as education, healthcare, infrastructure, and upholding the rule of law. This is especially critical in Africa’s diverse nations, fostering unity and shared goals.” The new AAPAM–eLearnLXD Scholarship Initiative directly addresses these challenges by providing affordable access to digital learning opportunities that equip public officials with advanced managerial, policy, and leadership skills needed to drive transformation across Africa’s governance institutions. Empowering Africa’s Public Sector through Digital Education The collaboration between AAPAM and eLearnLXD seeks to equip Africa’s public administrators and policymakers with the competencies required to strengthen governance, improve policy implementation, and enhance institutional performance. The University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN) Online MPA, delivered through the eLearnAfricaLXD Learning Management System (LMS), combines academic rigor with practical relevance. Its curriculum integrates key areas such as public policy, strategic management, human resource management, public finance, ethics in governance, and research methodology — preparing graduates to lead transformation within their organizations and communities. Prof. Chikelue Ofuebe, Professor of Public Administration and Local Government and former Director, Directorate of International Collaboration, University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), emphasized the transformative impact of the initiative, stating: “The University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), is a land-grant institution created to recruit and nurture well-grounded intellectuals with enormous capacity for innovative problem-solving strategies in the world. Consequently, her Online MPA programme stands as an ingenious Afrocentric model for purposeful collaboration in effective and efficient human capital development fit for the global community. As a result, with AAPAM and eLearnLXD, UNN is synergetically linking the expertise of African scholars, professionals, and the diaspora to create a shared platform for critical leadership development. This partnership embodies Africa’s collective commitment to strengthening governance, accountability, and service delivery through inclusive digital education. Therefore, without hesitation, I strongly encourage aspiring public sector leaders and other intellectually minded personalities and organizations to take advantage of this opportunity offered by the UNN Online MPA programme to acquire and utilize the skills, values, and global perspectives needed to drive meaningful change in the private and public sectors in the global community.” Beyond Scholarships: Knowledge Sharing and Collaboration In addition to scholarship opportunities, the partnership will also organize information sessions and webinars to engage stakeholders, share insights, and promote collaboration in the field of public administration. It will further facilitate research, joint publications, and dissemination of best practices in online learning, leadership development, and public sector management. These initiatives are designed to foster a continent-wide learning ecosystem that strengthens capacity, accountability, and innovation across Africa’s public service institutions. TITLE: Call for Expressions of Interest:  Participation in a Computational & Artificial Intelligence Engagement Planning Workshop

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The IEEE Computational Intelligence Society (CIS) and the Association of African Universities (AAU) aim to develop a program for stakeholders in Africa to increase their engagement in computational and artificial intelligence (AI). This program is motivated by the limited participation of African academics in computational and artificial intelligence – in comparison to the rest of the world. This is evidenced, for example, by the comparatively low numbers of papers submitted and/or published at premier AI conferences and journals by African authors. In addition, to date, there has been limited ‘bottom-up’ activity to establish support and engagement mechanisms such as via IEEE CIS membership and academic community engagement such as via CIS Chapters across most of Africa. As its overall outcome, the program targets an increase in CI/AI engagement, evidenced including through increased activity such as submission/publication of papers, CIS memberships, and Chapters from the African continent, including from academic, industry, and government stakeholders. This Call for Expression of Interest The AAU and the IEEE CIS are calling for academics based in Ghana, Liberia, Sierra Leone, and The Gambia that are keen to be involved in the computational and artificial intelligence program of activities, to respond to this call. The academics that are being targeted include: Lecturers, researchers and professors whose speciality is broadly in computer science, engineering, STEM and related areas. Recent PhD graduates / post-docs and PhD students whose speciality is broadly in computer science, engineering, STEM and related areas. Successful applicants will be engaged in an initial, virtual planning workshop with the following objectives: Discuss and establish local priorities in the field of computational and artificial intelligence. Discuss existing barriers and identify primary needs/ requirements/ activities which would be of benefit to support improved engagement with computational and artificial intelligence (CI/AI). Discuss existing engagement programs run by IEEE CIS, including: IEEE CIS International Mentoring Program IEEE CIS Paper Development Workshop Jointly co-design a plan for a range of engagement activities to be organised at future events. Targeted Outcomes of this planning workshop A list of identified local stakeholders who are interested in attending and/or contributing to future engagement activities, including through hosting such events. A plan for future joint CIS-AAU CI/AI engagement activities for both established and new stakeholders in Africa, complete with associated timeframe, planned activities, and location(s). How to submit the Expression of Interest Interested academics are requested to submit their interests by completing the online form via this link: https://forms.office.com/r/15EnwAfDP5 Deadlines and Notification of Acceptance The deadline for submission of the expressions of interest is close of business on Friday, 6th April 2024. We aim to send notification of acceptance to the planning workshop within three weeks of the above submission deadline. Contact Information If you have any queries concerning this call, please contact the Association of African Universities through Ms Nodumo Dhlamini on email: ndhlamini@aau.org with a copy to amsulemana@aau.org

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Western Balkans Fund (WBF) MOVE Grants 7th Open Call 2026 is now accepting applications from eligible individuals across the Western Balkans who are seeking financial support for short-term regional mobility, professional development, academic and scientific exchange, cultural cooperation, and sustainable development initiatives. Through the MOVE Grants Scheme, the Western Balkans Fund aims to strengthen people-to-people connections and regional cooperation by enabling individuals to travel beyond their country or place of residence to participate in meaningful learning, collaboration, exchange and representation opportunities. The programme is particularly relevant to artists, cultural professionals, researchers, scholars, journalists, youth workers, civil society activists, students, professionals and other changemakers who want to develop their skills, expand their networks and collaborate with individuals and institutions elsewhere in the Western Balkans. Successful applicants can request between €500 and €3,000, with the Western Balkans Fund able to cover up to 100% of eligible costs associated with an approved mobility activity. Applications for the 7th Open Call must be submitted by 5 October 2026 at 12:59 CET. About the Western Balkans Fund MOVE Grants Scheme The Western Balkans Fund developed the MOVE Grants mechanism around the principle that direct, in-person interaction can play an important role in strengthening trust, mutual understanding and shared values across the Western Balkans. The Western Balkans region covered by the programme consists of six WBF Contracting Parties: Albania Bosnia and Herzegovina Kosovo Montenegro North Macedonia Serbia Despite progress in regional cooperation, the Western Balkans continues to face challenges surrounding social cohesion, connectivity and deeper regional integration. MOVE Grants seek to contribute to addressing these challenges by making relatively small and accessible mobility grants available directly to individuals. Rather than focusing solely on large organisations and institutional projects, the scheme enables individual professionals, students and changemakers to pursue short-term opportunities that can produce meaningful professional and regional connections. The programme therefore places considerable emphasis on mobility, exchange and people-to-people cooperation. What Is the Main Objective of the MOVE Grants? The overall objective of the MOVE Grants Scheme is to foster regional cooperation in the Western Balkans by supporting individual mobility initiatives that promote: Academic exchange; Cultural exchange; Professional exchange; Regional collaboration; Learning and skills development; Knowledge sharing; Networking and partnership building; and Representation of the Western Balkans in relevant regional and international settings. Through short-term and needs-based opportunities for collaboration, representation and learning, the Western Balkans Fund seeks to strengthen people-to-people connections and cultivate a stronger regional mindset. The broader ambition is to empower individuals to become agents of positive change while contributing towards a more inclusive, equitable and interconnected Western Balkans. How Much Funding Is Available? The overall financial envelope available under the MOVE Grants 7th Open Call is €40,000. Individual applicants can request: Minimum grant: €500 Maximum grant: €3,000 The Western Balkans Fund may finance up to 100% of the total eligible costs of an approved mobility action. Cost-sharing or co-financing is also permitted where applicable. Applicants should develop realistic budgets based on genuine expected costs in the market. The budget should be prepared in euros and clearly connected to the proposed mobility activity. Only costs presented in the submitted budget will be considered for financing. Who Are MOVE Grants Designed to Support? MOVE Grants are intended for a diverse group of individuals from across the Western Balkans. Potential applicants include both young and senior professionals, such as: Individual artists; Cultural professionals; Researchers; Scholars; Journalists; Youth workers; Civil society organisation activists; Students; Established professionals; Professionals affiliated with public or non-public organisations; and Other changemakers whose mobility aligns with the objectives of the programme.
